strokeOrder: draw the high horizontal from left to right
without lifting, turn back down and left through the diagonal
without lifting, round the broad lower curve and sweep right to the finish
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03067 file records で as three stroke paths in this order and direction: て's stroke (the one stroke), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are two pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03067.svg, hiragana で (U+3067 HIRAGANA LETTER DE), three stroke paths kvg:03067-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is て's stroke, the same paths as in its file for て, kanji/03066.svg; s2 and s3 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.

notes: て voiced. Opens でんわ, a telephone, でんしゃ, a train, and でぐち, an exit.
